newsitem.title: USA: Ryder posts loss after restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Ryder posts loss after restructuring.

text.p: Ryder System, Inc. Tuesday reported a loss for the fourth quarter and full-year 1996, as expected, after the company took a major charge to restructure its struggling truck rental operations.
In January, the Miami-based company said it would take a pretax charge of $215 million in the fourth quarter to slash 2,100 jobs and dispose of nearly 200 facilities.

Ryder reported a net loss of $109.4 million, or $1.34 per share, for the quarter ended Dec. 31, compared with profits of $56.4 million, or 71 cents per share, in the 1995 period. Revenues rose to $1.36 billion from $1.35 billion.
For full-year 1996, the company lost $41.3 million, or 51 cents per share, compared with profits of $147.7 million, or $1.86 per share, in 1995. Revenue edged up to $5.52 billion from $5.17 billion.
The results include an after-tax gain of $15.1 million, or 18 cents per share, on the sale of Ryder's consumer truck rental business in October.

The restructuring, which cut fourth-quarter results by $143.6 million after taxes, was aimed largely at Ryder Transportation Services, whose commercial truck rental revenue and margins had declined. Restructuring charges totalled $163.9 million for the year.
In response to weak demand for rental trucks, Ryder Transportation slashed the size of its commercial truck rental fleet by more than 12 percent.
Ryder also took a one-time after-tax loss of $10 million to pay off debt early at a premium.

Ryder's 1996 performance was hurt as its Automotive Carrier Services division's largest customer suffered two strikes. The unit has been unable to pass on higher fuel costs and contractual driver wages to its customers.
In October, Ryder said it hired an adviser to explore strategic options for the Automotive Carrier unit.

The company's international operations went from a small profit in 1995 to a loss in 1996 as business in Britain came under significant pressure from competition in the truck leasing business. Startup costs also ate into profits in countries where Ryder has recently begun operations.
Ryder's stock edged up 12.5 cents to $28.75 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
